Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency. Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad. title: Business Operations Manager
description:
This is a remote position.   
 Business Operations Manager  Remote (India) | Full-time 
 Also searched as: Operations Manager, Business Operations Lead, PMO Manager, Project Operations Manager, Shared Services Manager, GCC Operations Manager.  Could you lead ops coordinators, project managers and service teams while carrying real projects alongside them? On a typical day you might run the planning call for a cross-team project you are leading, review a dashboard showing which requests are running late, sit with a pod lead to rebuild an estimate that looks twice as long as the last similar job, and agree with the Internal Product team which manual handoff to automate next. 
 About Contour  
 We operate across three brands. The India team, part of the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building. It runs delivery, automation, people and operations for the whole organisation, working closely with teams in Australia. 
 
 The kind of people who thrive here  Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on. Today we are about 600 people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing.  The work matters. More than 10,000 students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. People who do well here care about that. They own their work end to end, start things without being asked and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, write decisions down and give direct feedback. The pace is fast: small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle. Growth follows what you deliver: scope, title and pay move with the bar you raise.  About this role You lead Operations in Contour's India team: several teams brought together under one player-coach. Your team includes Contour’s operations coordinators, who keep academics, campus, finance and the founder’s office running day to day, and its project coordinators and managers, who run cross-team work across the business. It also covers organisation services such as print operations, procurement and workspace systems. Each service has two sides. In Australia, a functional owner, such as Finance or Academics, sets its standards and priorities. In India, you run the work: coordinators and project managers report to you directly, and any service big enough for its own pod lead reports through them. Everything else is yours: how work comes in, how it is planned, checked and automated, and how the people doing it grow. Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you learn each service's workflow well enough to coach its lead, inspect what it produces and challenge its estimates, and you know where your knowledge stops: on professional questions, you rely on the specialists. Second, you make different services run as one, with a shared way of taking requests, planning capacity and checking work, so the rest of Contour deals with one group rather than a row of separate desks. This is a player-coach seat, and we mean it. Expect a real share of most weeks to go on doing the work yourself: running a cross-team project end to end, taking the coordination nobody else can untangle, checking a sample of finished work, mapping a process that keeps stalling or rebuilding an estimate from the ground up. The rest goes on making your coordinators, project managers and pod leads better at the same work. You won't be the specialist in every service, but you can work inside each one's workflow, and your team sees you do it. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: the scope of this seat grows with the platform, and what you deliver decides how fast. The intake, planning, quality and automation routines you set now are what every later service joins. What you will do 
 
 
 Run work yourself: lead some cross-team projects and coordination directly, especially the messy ones, so you know first-hand what your team is up against. 
 
 Lead the coordinators and project managers: set how projects and department requests are scoped, tracked and closed, review their plans and status updates, and step in when work slips. 
 
 Map every service's workflow with the people who run it and document it in Notion so anyone can follow it. 
 
 Run one front door for requests: a single intake form with clear turnaround times, so the rest of Contour deals with one group. 
 
 Plan capacity weekly using live dashboards of demand, turnaround and backlog, not gut feel. 
 
 Automate the repeatable: spot manual handoffs, data entry and status chasing, and work with the Internal Product team to automate them (for example with Monday, Notion, Slack, Google Workspace or no-code tools). 
 
 Use AI where it saves time: first-pass quality checks, drafting SOPs, summarising requests, with people keeping the final call.

 Familiarity with French vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling conventions (including verlan, regional expressions, and English influences).

Because you will sell and serve the same region, you own the full customer journey: from first demo to go-live, adoption and renewal.    What you'll do      Customer success (about 50%)

 5+ years of experience across pre-sales or solutions engineering, customer success and account management, in B2B SaaS or retail technology.

 A self-starter who works well remotely, across time zones, and is comfortable building processes in a region we are still growing.

 Portuguese, for customers and prospects in Brazil.

 Shape how  Quicklizard  sells to and serves customers across the Americas, at an early stage of our growth in the region.

title: Senior Data Engineer, Embedded
description:
Opportunity is not evenly distributed.  Shopify  puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to 10,000 employees and generated over $496 billion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries. This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option. 
 About You 
 
 Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means  Shopify  is not the right place for everyone. 
 Before you apply, consider if you can: 
 
 Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone 
 Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth 
 Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter) 
 Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change 
 Bring critical thought and opinion 
 Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward 
 Work digital-first for your daily work 
 
 
 About the role 
  Data is a crucial part of  Shopify ’s mission to make commerce better for everyone. We organize and interpret petabytes of data to provide solutions for our merchants and stakeholders across the organization.  As a Data Engineer at  Shopify , your primary responsibility will be to contribute to  Shopify ’s Data Warehouse. Your work will unlock powerful insights to guide the development and improvement of  Shopify ’s products. As an embedded Data Engineer, you will work directly building foundations for products that transform merchants' lives. You'll collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of professionals that can include Product Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Business Analysts, and Product Management. The data you shape will be used to power product analysis, dashboards, and reports. You will also contribute by performing product analysis and creating dashboards and reports yourself from time to time. Get excited about flexing these analysis and reporting muscles, while also evangelizing the values and excellence in the Data Engineering craft to your multidisciplinary peers in a fast moving environment with competing priorities. Our product is designed to empower entrepreneurs. Consequently, the work you do will not only create value for our users but also contribute to global entrepreneurship. To thrive here, you need to be dedicated to your craft and committed to constant development. You should be an independent thinker who can solve complex problems and handle a bit of chaos without breaking a sweat.  Example day to day responsibilities include:  
 
 Working with business partners to understand business and product objectives and identify the data needed to support them 
 Designing, building, implementing, and documenting data models 
 Writing data transformations using dbt or Spark 
 Shipping data pipelines including real-time streaming and batch processing 
 Optimizing data transformation pipelines to increase freshness or reduce computational time/cost 
 Working with engineers to understand and influence how data is produced  
 Collaborating with other data engineers on tooling for automated tasks around consuming, validating raw/modeled data, updating modeled data 
 Subscribing to and implementing architecture and standards following the Data Engineer craft at  Shopify 
 
 Collaborating with sister disciplines (Engineering, Data Science) to establish best practices and evangelize the values and priorities of the Data Engineering craft 
 Partnering closely with product, engineering and other business leaders to influence product and program decisions with data 
 Building production-quality dashboards and scalable data products 
 
 
 Qualifications 
  
 Commercial experience in Data Engineering, and/or Analytics Engineering, ​​​​​​building scalable data warehouses 
 Dimensional Modeling (Star Schema, Kimball, Inmon) 
 Advanced SQL skills (ease with window functions, defining UDFs) 
 Exposure to Data Engineering tooling: ingesting, testing transformations, lineage, orchestration, publishing data, metric layers 
 Hands-on experience implementing real-time and batch data pipelines with tight SLOs and complex transformation requirements 
 Fantastic collaboration and communication skills, demonstrated by successful large-scale projects spanning multiple teams 
 Technical thought leader, comfortable navigating ambiguity and mentoring various level of team members 
 Aptitude for product analysis, dashboarding, and reporting

title: Distributed Systems Engineer, Multi-Chip Simulation (Mid/Senior/Principal)
description:
About Positron AI    Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.   
   Role Overview   
 Running one AI model across many chips is a distributed systems problem: a host and many chips exchanging data over links, waiting on each other, and failing in ways no single chip would. As a Senior Distributed Systems Engineer, you will help us simulate that system before the hardware exists. You will work with the chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams to build the simulators that stand in for the host, the links, and the protocols between chips. 
 This role is about building and scaling simulation infrastructure, not testing someone else's code. You will own the software architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack, decide how much fidelity each layer needs, and keep it fast enough that distributed software is exercised every day in CI. 
   Key Responsibilities   
   Multi-Chip Simulator Design   
 
 Design and build the simulators for the host-to-chip and chip-to-chip layers of our system, including the drivers, links, protocols, and transfers that connect many chips into one machine. 
 Model the communication fabric, including transfer timing, collectives, ordering guarantees, back-pressure, congestion, and partial failure, calibrated against real hardware. 
 
   Architecture and Scale   
 
 Own the architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack as new chips, interconnects, and deployment topologies arrive. 
 Compose simulators of different fidelity (fast functional, cycle-level, and hardware emulation) into one coherent multi-chip simulation. 
 Scale the simulation from a few chips to full racks while keeping runs fast enough for daily use in CI. 
 
   Correlation and Quality   
  Correlate simulated behavior against emulation and hardware measurements, with regression coverage and clear documentation of assumptions and limitations.  
   Required Qualifications   
 
 5+ years of experience as a distributed systems engineer building and operating software that coordinates many machines or accelerators through RPC, message passing, consensus, or collective communication. 
 A strong understanding of the failure modes of distributed software, including races, partial failure, ordering and consistency, timeouts and retries, back-pressure, and deadlock. 
 Demonstrated experience debugging timing-dependent bugs across hosts, NICs, or accelerators using traces and logs. 
 Experience building simulators, emulators, or test harnesses for distributed or networked systems is strongly preferred. 
 Sound judgment in choosing the right level of fidelity for a question and balancing accuracy against run time. 
 Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for tooling and analysis. 
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain what the simulation shows, what it does not, and what the software or hardware team should change. 
 
   Preferred Qualifications   
 
 Hands-on experience with multi-GPU or multi-accelerator inference or training, including NCCL-style collectives, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism, and host-device runtimes. 
 Familiarity with hardware emulators such as Cadence Palladium or Synopsys ZeBu, or with FPGA prototyping.

Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

 You will own the architecture of the simulation stack that lets our distributed software run across racks of chips long before the hardware exists. 
 You will work across chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams on one of the hardest problems in AI inference: making many chips behave as one machine.

You'll work alongside designers, IT, and MarTech to build solutions that serve real business needs while protecting each brand's unique identity.

 Stay current on emerging web standards and bring ideas to the table where they genuinely fit.

 4+ years of front-end web development experience, with strong skills in semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and WordPress. 
 The ability to build a custom WordPress theme from scratch using PHP templates and Advanced Custom Fields. 
 Strong CSS skills across Sass and modern native CSS (custom properties, nesting), and solid vanilla JavaScript. 
 Comfort working in Git/GitHub with pull requests and code reviews, and with npm-based build tools and the command line.
